topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, outlines the scope of the cancer lecture series, and sets out the key learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Foundations of Cancer Etiology, Risk Factors, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core concepts of cancer development, examining the balance between intrinsic random mutations and environmental exposures through global epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents contribute to oncogenesis, detailing the specific mechanism and geographical co-factors of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe specific physical and chemical mutagens and detail how host xenobiotic metabolism can convert unreactive compounds into DNA-damaging adducts.

topics.label: Tumor Promoters, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish non-mutagenic tumor promoters from initiators, explaining how chronic inflammation, aberrant signaling pathways, and host developmental timing create permissive environments for malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Mutational Signatures and Genomic Profiling
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how whole-genome sequencing reveals characteristic mutational signatures that link specific DNA damage patterns back to particular carcinogenic exposures.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing Carcinogenicity and Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine carcinogenicity, concluding with the practical challenges of assessing potency and balancing risk.
